subject: Why fixed=TRUE vs. FALSE in Multinomial Models

messages.author: e7014f74b5d49111
messages.subject: Why fixed=TRUE vs. FALSE in Multinomial Models
parts:
I am still trying to figure out the Multinomial Model I posted here


One question that came up:

In the multinomial example in the FAQ they specify fixed=TRUE within the hyper component of the f() function. 

However in the alli.R code this is not specified and defaults to fixed=FALSE. 

Why the difference? Really the question is what is fixed=TRUE vs fixed=FALSE doing? Could someone please give a simplified example?

One thing I note is that when I switch my code from fixed=TRUE to fixed=FALSE the sample names I get with inla.posterior.sample end up being different. Any idea why this is?

Thank you very much,
Justin Silverman

messages.author: 9940b4fcc153c7d7
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Why fixed=TRUE vs. FALSE in Multinomial Models
parts:
fixed=T 
You are no longer doing inference on the hyper-parameter, but just fixing it to the initial value. If you look at the two summaries for the two results (with and without fixed=T), you see that one of them has fewer posteriors for hyper-parameters. 

Regards,
Haakon
